criteria.text: The company offers buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) consumer products that let shoppers defer payment or split purchases into installments at checkout.
criteria.rationale: BNPL product capability is the core functional distinction between Klarna-like peers and generic payment or fintech firms that do not provide consumer installment credit at checkout.

criteria.text: The company provides merchant-facing e-commerce integrations (for example checkout plugins, APIs, or SDKs) to embed BNPL at the point of sale.
criteria.rationale: Klarna-like peers integrate directly into merchant checkouts; this separates platform/integration providers from consumer-only finance apps or banks that do not integrate with online merchants.

criteria.text: The company serves e-commerce merchants and online shoppers as primary customers.
criteria.rationale: Serving both merchants and consumers in e-commerce distinguishes BNPL vendors from lenders that focus only on consumers or payment processors that target non-retail verticals.

criteria.text: The company operates in one or more European countries.
criteria.rationale: The user explicitly requested European BNPLs; requiring European operations filters out geographically non-relevant BNPL providers.

criteria.text: The company provides merchant settlement or a payment guarantee (i.e., it pays merchants for transactions while collecting repayment from consumers over time).
criteria.rationale: Many Klarna-like competitors differentiate by taking merchant settlement risk or guaranteeing merchant payouts, which separates them from platforms that only broker third-party consumer credit without guaranteeing merchant payment.
